hypothesis: The ~36 auth.json lock cycles per fresh first turn (model-resolve-cache record 20260927-013300, reported-only; #2915 serialized same-process holders but the cycles remained) come from per-call AuthStorage rebuilds: every AuthStorage::create runs a full with_lock file-protocol cycle (exclusive-create openat, mkdir auth.json.lock, utimensat probe, read, rmdir) even when the document has not changed. TS keeps ONE AuthStorage per session-services instance (agent-session-services.ts:164, shared with ModelRegistry + McpManager) and serves getApiKey from its in-memory snapshot - zero per-turn lock cycles. A storage-layer read-through content cache (a pure-read trait arm, stat-validated per path) should collapse the per-call read cycles to one miss per process per document with byte-identical file-protocol behavior for every writer and the port's per-call freshness preserved (any external atomic-rename write changes the inode; an in-place rewrite moves the mtime).
approach: Baseline decomposition first (no code changes): 31 trials on one VM at 9b62f26af (12 fresh 1-turn + 8 fresh 2-turn timing legs, controls, 3 strace legs, 2 diagnostic-build census legs with an env-gated pid/tid backtrace at FileAuthStorageBackend::with_lock; bench compare.msg_send mock-regime protocol replicated verbatim from the model-resolve-cache lane incl. 120x40 PTY, probe-input-ready, typed prompt, Enter->first-chunk ack, needle+600ms-stability settle, PI_REQUEST_TIMING on; I/O advisory v1.0 preflights at every leg boundary). Candidate = 2 commits: C1 the read-through cache (auth/storage.rs + manager.rs), C2 the settings same-process mutex (settings/storage.rs, the #2915 pattern). ABBA phase 1: 2-arm pair base vs C1 found a REGRESSION (+10.5ms p50, 3/6 stall legs); mechanism analysis attributed it to the settings storage's pre-existing same-process lock contention unmasked by removing the auth cycles' accidental pacing. ABBA phase 2: 3-ARM ATTRIBUTION (base / C1 / C1+C12=C12) with census pairs; ABBA phase 3: confirmation pair at the PR head (folded tip base e6e7a26e4 vs PR head 7d4dce037). Same-VM sequential, sha-asserted binaries per leg, order-balanced rounds, unique per-leg output paths, zombie sweeps.
parity_notes: Frozen parity untouched: the file protocol (proper-lockfile mkdir/utimensat/stale-reclaim/rmdir), the 10x20ms retry structure, settings protocol, session JSONL, RLM wire, prompts, TUI behavior all unchanged. with_lock (every write and read-modify-write flow, incl. mcp_command's direct backend use) is byte-for-byte unchanged. The pure-read arm (AuthStorageBackend::read, default = the old with_lock read) is used ONLY by AuthStorage::reload. TS-parity case FIRST: TS constructs ONE AuthStorage per session services instance and reads its in-memory snapshot per turn (agent-session-services.ts:164, ModelRegistry.create(authStorage,...), new McpManager({authStorage,...})); the port mirrors the TS create() shape at ~45 call sites where TS reuses the single instance - the per-call rebuild is a port artifact with no TS counterpart benefit (each instance re-reads the same unchanged file). The stat-validated cache keeps the port's per-call freshness STRICTLY fresher than the TS snapshot instance (an external write invalidates on the next read; TS never re-reads). R8 preserved: fresh startup-chain resolutions see exactly what they see today (the stat identity guarantees byte-identity; the resolution call sites are untouched). Documented behavior delta: a cache hit now succeeds under a foreign lock holder while the document is unchanged (TS serves its snapshot in exactly that window); first reads in a process (cache misses) keep the old contention behavior. No callback re-entrancy: the read arm has no callback; the settings mutex is a leaf (every settings callback is a pure JSON transform - verified at all 6 production call sites).

outcome: POSITIVE with a disclosed regression-discovery arc: the auth read-through cache collapses the per-fresh-first-turn auth.json lock cycles 36 -> 2 (census-verified at the pre-fold base, in the 3-arm attribution, and at the PR head), worth ~6ms/turn of lock-protocol wall cost on the session-open path and -1.5ms submit->assistant_row p50; the 2-arm ABBA honestly surfaced that the cache UNMASKS the settings storage's pre-existing same-process lock contention (the auth cycles' 150-300us same-process serialization was pacing worker threads apart by accident; the class existed in the base at 1/12 - the baseline decomposition's own 22ms slow dispatch) raising it to 5/12 stall legs; the #2915-pattern settings mutex (authorized companion) eliminates the class entirely (0 overlaps, 0 sleeps, 0 stall legs in the C12 arm) while keeping the cache's win: assistant_row p50 7.72 -> 6.24ms, reply p50 29.85 -> 28.75ms, stall legs 1/12 -> 0/6, distribution tight [5.9..12.7] vs [5.8..25.4]; confirmation at the PR head re-verifies (9.04 -> 6.86ms p50 at a DEGRADED-fresh window, auth cycles 36/44 -> 2/2).
decision: Lane evidence complete at the PR head 7d4dce037 (PR #2932): the 3-arm attribution shows the unmasking mechanism AND the fix in one evidence set (A 1/12 stalls, C1 5/12 - the auth win visible at -1.6ms but the stall tail surfaces, C12 0/6 stalls + the lowest reply p50 + census 0/0/0/0). Claim scope: (1) auth-lock cycle consolidation 36 -> ~3 per fresh first turn across the process tree (1 miss per process per document + stat-validated hits), with byte-identical file protocol for all writers and the port's per-call freshness preserved; (2) the settings same-process contention class (pre-existing at base rate, unmasked by any auth-path speedup) removed by the #2915-pattern mutex. Reported-only for future lanes: settings.json is lock-cycled 32-43x per fresh first turn (per-call SettingsManager rebuilds - the same structural pattern as the auth finding; the mutex serializes but does not consolidate). Frozen parity surfaces untouched: session JSONL, RLM wire, prompts, TUI bytes, the file protocols.
